proposed.text: Why would a government employee choose GSIS housing loans as an alternative to Pag-IBIG, even though both are available?

options.text: GSIS loans are the only option for government employees, as Pag-IBIG does not cater to their specific needs
Pag-IBIG is not available to government employees, making GSIS the default choice
GSIS loans may offer different terms, rates, or benefits as an ancillary service to GSIS insurance members, providing an alternative to Pag-IBIG
GSIS loans have no interest and are government-subsidized grants, making them financially advantageous

proposed.rationale: While Pag-IBIG is the primary option, GSIS housing loans provide an alternative pathway with potentially different terms, rates, tenure, or processing criteria. Having multiple lenders increases competition and borrower choice. [A]: Government employees have multiple options (Pag-IBIG and GSIS). [B]: Pag-IBIG is mandatory and available to all employees, including government workers. [C]: While Pag-IBIG is the primary option, GSIS housing loans provide an alternative pathway with potentially different terms, rates, tenure, or processing criteria. Having multiple lenders increases competition and borrower choice. [D]: GSIS loans are credit products with interest, not grants.
proposed.explanation: Government employees have multiple options (Pag-IBIG and GSIS). Pag-IBIG is mandatory and available to all employees, including government workers. While Pag-IBIG is the primary option, GSIS housing loans provide an alternative pathway with potentially different terms, rates, tenure, or processing criteria. Having multiple lenders increases competition and borrower choice. GSIS loans are credit products with interest, not grants. While Pag-IBIG is the primary option, GSIS housing loans provide an alternative pathway with potentially different terms, rates, tenure, or processing criteria. Having multiple lenders increases competition and borrower choice. Multiple finance sources (Pag-IBIG + GSIS for government employees) = borrower choice.
